modules.title: 两个库存请求怎样持有、等待并释放锁
锁怎样给共享记录建立访问顺序

items.title: 问题与关键机制
items.text: 两个请求都读到库存 1 并各自扣减时可能超卖；给共享库存记录加锁，让一个请求完成检查和修改，另一个等待后再检查。

items.title: 改善看等待后的新判断
items.text: 并发测试应得到一个成功、一个库存不足，最终库存为 0；锁保证访问顺序，但加锁顺序不一致仍可能造成死锁，跨实例范围也要确认。

items.title: 第二个场景：诊室排班
items.text: 两个工作人员同时安排同一诊室时段时，锁应覆盖同一时段记录；先完成者释放后，等待者重新检查，避免两场预约占用同一时段。

modules.title: 容易混淆的地方
modules.text: 锁只保护它实际覆盖的共享资源和范围。错误的加锁顺序可能造成死锁；一把进程内锁不会自动跨多个服务实例生效，等待超时和释放路径也必须处理。

lessonPractice.title: 库存只剩 1 件，两个后端实例同时扣减。哪种加锁判断最可靠？

options.label: 使用能保护同一数据库记录的锁，持有者完成后让等待者重新检查库存
options.feedback: 对。锁的作用范围要覆盖两个竞争者共同访问的资源，等待者取得锁后仍需基于新状态判断。

options.label: 在每个实例各自创建一把进程内锁，就认定两个实例已经互斥
options.feedback: 不同实例的进程内锁彼此不可见，不能自动保护同一数据库记录。

options.label: 两个请求先各自扣减库存，写完以后再取得锁记录结果
options.feedback: 冲突已经发生；锁必须覆盖检查和修改共享资源的临界区。

en.title: Only one item remains and two backend instances decrement it concurrently. Which lock decision is reliable?

options.label: Use a lock that protects the same database record, then make the waiter recheck stock
options.feedback: Correct. The lock scope covers the shared resource, and a waiter evaluates the new state after acquiring it.

options.label: Create one in-process lock per instance and assume the instances now exclude each other
options.feedback: Separate in-process locks cannot see each other and do not protect one shared database record.

options.label: Let both requests decrement first, then acquire a lock to record what happened
options.feedback: The conflict has already happened; the lock must cover the check-and-update critical section.

lessonAgentPrompt.title: 你可以这样告诉 AI Agent
lessonAgentPrompt.text: 请为库存扣减加锁，锁的范围必须覆盖同一条库存记录的检查和修改。记录持有者、等待者、释放和超时；用两个并发请求测试只允许一个成功，另一个取得锁后重新检查并返回库存不足。若服务有多个实例，不要只用各自的进程内锁。

en.title: You can say this to an AI Agent
en.text: Lock the inventory check and update for the same shared record. Record owner, waiter, release, and timeout. Test two concurrent requests so only one succeeds and the waiter rechecks after acquiring the lock and returns out of stock. If the service has multiple instances, do not rely only on separate in-process locks.

learning.assumes: You know requests can update the same database record or memory object concurrently.
learning.outcome: You can name the shared resource and lock scope, then verify ownership, waiting, release, and final state.

modules.title: How two inventory requests own, wait for, and release a lock
How a lock orders access to a shared record

items.title: Problem and key mechanism
items.text: Both requests can read stock 1 and decrement it, causing overselling; lock the shared inventory record so one request checks and updates while the other waits and then rechecks.

items.title: Verify the waiter rechecks
items.text: Concurrent testing yields one success, one out-of-stock result, and final stock 0. Cross-instance scope and deadlock still need handling.

items.title: A second scenario: clinic scheduling
items.text: When two staff members schedule the same clinic room and time slot, the lock should cover that shared slot. After the first releases it, the waiter rechecks so two appointments cannot occupy the same slot.

modules.title: What people often confuse
modules.text: A lock protects only the resource and scope it actually covers. Inconsistent order can deadlock, and one in-process lock does not coordinate separate service instances. Timeout and release paths also matter.

distinctions.label: Race Condition
distinctions.text: {c:race-condition} is the concurrency anomaly caused by unpredictable timing; a {c:lock} is a synchronization primitive used to prevent race conditions.

distinctions.label: Lease
distinctions.text: A {c:lock} requires manual release; a {c:lease} is a distributed lock variant with automatic expiration and renewal.
